2609.11545.title: Complex-Text Robustness Evaluation and Failure Diagnosis for Low-Resource Multilingual Text-to-Speech
2609.11545.paper_summary: Low-resource multilingual text-to-speech (TTS) systems have expanded language coverage, but their robustness under complex text inputs remains insufficiently diagnosed. Existing evaluations mainly focus on naturalness, speaker similarity, and content consistency using regular test sentences, while providing limited insight into how multilingual TTS systems fail when handling challenging inputs such as numbers, dates, named entities, long sentences, code-switched expressions, and punctuation-related structures. This paper proposes a complex-text robustness diagnosis framework for low-resource multilingual TTS. We evaluate robustness from three dimensions: content consistency, language consistency, and generation stability. A multilingual robustness testing scheme is designed for Thai, Vietnamese, Swahili, and Indonesian, covering ordinary sentences and multiple types of complex text inputs. We further introduce automatic diagnostic metrics, including character error rate, language identification accuracy, and duration abnormal rate. To support input-level risk analysis before speech generation, we propose a lightweight Text Risk Score (TRS), which estimates synthesis risk from interpretable text features without manual annotation or model training. Experiments on three representative multilingual TTS systems, including OmniVoice, VoxCPM2, and MMS-TTS, show that complex text inputs expose systematic failure patterns that are not fully reflected by ordinary short-sentence evaluation. Different systems exhibit distinct vulnerabilities in number normalization, named entity handling, long-text generation, and code-switched input processing. Furthermore, TRS shows a positive correlation with content errors and duration abnormalities, demonstrating its usefulness as a low-cost pre-synthesis indicator for complex-text risk diagnosis in low-resource multilingual TTS.
2609.11545.paper_summary_zh: 低資源多語言文本轉語音（TTS）系統已擴展語言覆蓋範圍，但在複雜文本輸入下的穩健性仍然不足。<lb/>現有的評估主要集中在自然度、說話者相似性和內容一致性上，使用常規測試句子，對多語言 TTS 系統在處理挑戰性輸入（如數字、日期、命名實體、長句子、代碼切換表達和與標點符號相關的結構）時的失敗提供的見解有限。<lb/>本文提出了一個針對低資源多語言 TTS 的複雜文本穩健性診斷框架。<lb/>我們從三個維度評估穩健性：內容一致性、語言一致性和生成穩定性。<lb/>為泰語、越南語、斯瓦希里語和印尼語設計了一個多語言穩健性測試方案，涵蓋普通句子和多種類型的複雜文本輸入。<lb/>我們進一步引入自動診斷指標，包括字符錯誤率、語言識別準確率和持續異常率。<lb/>為了支持在語音生成之前的輸入級風險分析，我們提出了一種輕量級文本風險評分（TRS），它從可解釋的文本特徵中估算合成風險，而無需手動標註或模型訓練。<lb/>對三個具有代表性的多語言 TTS 系統（包括 OmniVoice、VoxCPM2 和 MMS-TTS）的實驗顯示，複雜文本輸入暴露了系統性失敗模式，而這些模式在普通短句評估中並未完全反映。<lb/>不同系統在數字標準化、命名實體處理、長文本生成和代碼切換輸入處理方面表現出不同的脆弱性。<lb/>此外，TRS 與內容錯誤和持續異常之間顯示出正相關，證明其作為低資源多語言 TTS 中複雜文本風險診斷的低成本前合成指標的有效性。
